text:
**My pick: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port (3× USB-C + 1× USB-A).** Two TechWise reviews rank it best overall for travel. Either of its first two USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone. With two devices the split is 65W + 30W, and with all four ports in use it's 45W, 30W and 10.5W on the rest. It's the heaviest of the group at 8.3 oz, and it supports PD 3.0, PPS and QC 4+. [TechWise GaN chargers review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) · [TechWise multi-device review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026)

**Other good options:**

- **Anker Prime 67W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A):** This is the smallest and lightest at about 4.78 oz. It supports PPS for Samsung and Pixel phones, and drops to about 65W when two devices are connected. It suits one laptop, one phone and one accessory. [VoyageHacks comparison](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/)
- **Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A):** This is the one to get if a power-hungry laptop is your priority. [TechWise multi-device review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026)
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A):** It costs $49.99 for a 2-pack, so you get one for home and one for your bag. It has foldable prongs and delivers 65W from either USB-C port alone. With two devices plugged in, the laptop port drops to 45W, which is fine for a MacBook Air but slower for a 65W laptop. Buy it here: [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W 2-pack](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) (affiliate link, and Dealectric's source said no discount code worked). That source had no Anker or UGREEN products, so it couldn't compare them. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-travel-charger-multiple-usb-c-ports-2026-anker-ugreen-reviews)

**Things to know:**
- The search results didn't include direct purchase links for the UGREEN or Anker chargers. The review pages above have "check price" buttons, and I can't confirm current prices for those.
- All of these have US prongs. For international trips you'll need a plug adapter, not a voltage converter, since they accept 100–240V.
- If you want the adapter built in, Android Central's picks include the [UGREEN 65W Nexode travel adapter](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel) (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A) and the Epicka TA-105 Max 75W (3× USB-C + 2× USB-A).
- Use a cable rated for the wattage you expect. A true 100W needs an e-marked 5A cable.

If you tell me what you're charging (laptop model, phone, etc.) and whether you travel abroad, I can narrow it down.
